body:
Context assembly now tracks exact compact JSON size from serialized entries, array commas and included/omitted decimal widths. Every source read, source version, structured field, warning, omission/hint, array cap and final full byte check remains.

Two quiet M4/macOS release series retain complete normalized control output for all 800 selected observations. Rich maximum-budget contexts save 25.2–25.3 ms (about 20%); ordinary maximum-budget contexts save 5.5–6.2 ms. Small/minimum contexts save only about 0.25 ms. This is context preparation evidence, without claiming universal UI or tail improvement.

The full gate passes 465 tests. An initial disk-space failure is resolved by discarding a worktree build cache and serializing independent Rust tests while retaining bounds and explicit concurrency checks. Normally paired Chromium/WebKit protocol tests pass full HTTP/CLI context equality, actual byte limits and invalid-budget rejection.

Application bfbb58dbf2a7671041451f6b4e9431fba5a42a8a is rebuilt and verified at the existing trusted HTTPS address. The restart preserves 72 prior source versions, two pins, settings, certificate, epoch and complete normalized CLI context; all 32 served assets match. The unrelated owner card remains unchanged. Broader perceived performance and platform/release acceptance remain open. Details: progress/2026-10-01-context-budget.md.

metadata.summary: Exact context JSON byte accounting reduces large-response CPU work
